subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-event taxonomy and manifest-gated plugin emission API as a permanent public plugin contract, and is the manifest rule intended as cooperative telemetry policy rather than isolation from malicious installed plugins?
rationale: The repository treats installed plugins as trusted in-process code, while this PR introduces a versioned operator-facing taxonomy and presents manifest declarations as an authorization boundary; implementation details cannot determine the intended long-term product and trust contract.

options.title: Sponsor a host-bound taxonomy
options.body: Approve the taxonomy direction but require the emitter, identity, manifest policy, validation, attribution, documentation, and proof to be host-owned and complete before merge.

options.title: Narrow to core-only events
options.body: Keep AI-safety events internal to trusted core producers and defer third-party plugin emission until a smaller plugin contract is designed.

options.title: Decline the taxonomy series
options.body: Keep existing diagnostic and security-event surfaces rather than adding a new permanent taxonomy and observability stack.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a host-bound taxonomy
recommendation.body: Approve the taxonomy direction but require the emitter, identity, manifest policy, validation, attribution, documentation, and proof to be host-owned and complete before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and related review context most directly connect this person to plugin manifest contracts and the product/security decision required here.
